question: Ascent — ATK pistol round, 5v5, no spike, 1:23 left. You hold a Sheriff pressed against the A Main wall, everyone still alive. What is the highest-EV pistol-round play here?

options.label: Hold your crosshair pre-aimed at head level on the A Main choke and take a disciplined first-tap if a defender peeks
options.explication_courte: Pistol rounds are decided by first bullets and armor math. Pre-aiming head-level at the choke with a Sheriff means one clean tap = one dead defender, swinging the round to a 5v4 before util or numbers even matter.

sources_option.citation: Pistol and eco rounds are won on first-shot discipline and armor value; pre-aim common angles and tap heads rather than spray

options.label: Peek out into A Main now to take space early while you have full HP
options.explication_courte: Peeking first on a pistol hands the defender the pre-aim advantage — they're already sighted on the choke and one tap trades you. On equal pistols, the peeker usually loses the opening duel.

sources_option.citation: The player holding a pre-aimed angle beats the player peeking into it; don't hand the defense the reaction advantage on a pistol

options.label: Wait for your team to group and default before you commit to any angle
options.explication_courte: Setting up a structured default is genuinely fine on a pistol — but sitting completely passive at the wall with a pre-aimable choke in front of you leaves free opening-pick equity on the table if a defender wanders into your angle.

sources_option.citation: A disciplined default spreads for info; but don't ignore a free angle you already control while waiting to group

options.label: Save your Sheriff by falling back to spawn and playing for the bonus round
options.explication_courte: There is nothing to save on a pistol round — everyone is on equal equipment. Conceding the pistol without a fight throws the single highest-swing round of the half and the bonus economy that follows it.

sources_option.citation: The pistol round has outsized economic swing; conceding it without contesting forfeits the round and the follow-on bonus

explication_longue: Pistol rounds swing on two things: who lands the first clean headshot, and the armor economy behind it. Pressed against the A Main wall with a Sheriff and everyone alive, your job is to convert the angle you already hold into a free opening pick. Pre-aiming head level at the A Main choke means the moment a defender peeks, your Sheriff — a one-tap-to-the-head weapon — turns the round into a 5v4 before numbers, utility, or a plant ever come into play. Peeking out first inverts that: you walk into whatever the defense has pre-aimed, and on equal pistols the peeker loses the reaction duel far more often than they win it. Playing a structured default with your team is a legitimate alternative and often correct — but it is not a reason to sit blind at the wall ignoring a choke you already control; hold the angle while your team spreads. Saving is simply wrong here: on a pistol everyone is on identical equipment, so there is no weapon worth preserving, and conceding the round forfeits both it and the bonus-round economy that a pistol win sets up. Hold, pre-aim, tap.

sources.citation: Win pistols with first-shot discipline, armor value and controlled angles; the pistol round has outsized economic swing
